messages:
nightly-evals-bot: nightly-evals: regression alert for model: redwood-v2-small-quant (canary) — metric: chrF (-6.2) / BLEU (-4.9) on 'multilang-translation' promptset. Details: https://prod-evals/reports/1748004823 :warning:

maya: saw it. JP and AR look especially bad. quick skim of failed examples below.

maya: ```source: ja
input: '明日のミーティングは午後3時に変更になりました。'
ref: 'The meeting was moved to 3 PM tomorrow.'
old_out: 'The meeting has been changed to 3:00 PM tomorrow.'
new_out: 'Tomorrow, the meeting will be shifted to the afternoon of three.'  <-- awkward, lost numeric tokenization and polite nuance
```

maya: ```source: ar
input: 'هل يمكنك إرسال التقرير قبل انتهاء اليوم؟'
ref: 'Can you send the report before the end of the day?'
old_out: 'Can you send the report before EOD?'
new_out: 'Can you send the report before the end of the day today?' <-- repeats, inserts extra temporal anchor, degrades concision
```

jin: ccing localization folks. JP polite register is off — model inserts uncommon phrasing. That could break product strings.

sam: hypothesis: this popped after we switched to int4-scaling kernel in the latest quant candidate (WIP). I've seen similar tokenization drift when per-channel scale changed. Can we confirm which binary was used for the nightly run?

leo: nightly-evals-bot: run metadata shows runtime_tag=canary-quant-int4-2025-07-14, model artifact=redwood-v2-small@rev-20250711, tokenizer=tokenizer-v3.

sam: ok that's the quant path. next steps: 1) re-run subset of the multilang promptset with float16 baseline + int8 quant to isolate; 2) capture log-prob distributions for JP/AR tokens; 3) diff tokenization for numeric and polite forms.

maya: I can run step 1 and 2 this afternoon. will push a diff eval and paste link. also I'll extract 50 worst failures per language.

jin: please include examples where translation inserted extra temporal anchors or changed register — product team needs clear repros.

leo: action items: @maya run targeted evals; @sam run tokenization diff script; @jin collect product-sensitive examples and flag strings to freeze. I'll create a tracking Jira: ML-TR-972 and add owners.

maya: started a targeted job: eval-job-1748005001 (float16 vs int4 vs int8). ETA ~ 45m. will post summary + top 50 CSV.

sam: while that's running: small check — can we grep for changes in softmax temperature or sampling config in the canary deploy? sometimes quantized kernels accidentally set fused-kv cache fallback that affects output determinism.

leo: checked deploy diff: no sampling config changes; only kernel and microbatch tuning. kernel change logs attached to the Jira.

nightly-evals-bot: eval-job-1748005001 completed. summary: float16 baseline retains prior metrics; int8 shows minor drop (chrF -1.1); int4 reproduces full regression (chrF -6.0). top failure examples uploaded: https://prod-evals/reports/1748005001/files

maya: upload complete. quick observation: tokenization mismatch at numerals and Arabic diacritics more frequent in int4 run. Also some outputs show unnecessary literal translations of honorifics in JP.

sam: looks like quant scale quantization is affecting embedding for small vocabulary tokens => downstream generation drift. plan: try tighter per-channel calibration or switch to per-tensor fallback for numeric tokens.

jin: product ask: if we need to roll back canary, we'll need a short blurb for customers in APAC/MENA about temporary model fallback. keep me posted.

leo: proposal: rollback canary-quant-int4 from hosted until we have a fix; keep it in Dedicated testing lane. I'll schedule rollback for next deploy window unless objections.

maya: +1 rollback. I'll continue to triage on int4 experiments and post a patch branch once I have calibration numbers.

sam: I'll prototype a calibration patch (per-channel forced recalibration + token whitelist for per-tensor) and run a small 1k-sample eval.

jin: thanks — please flag any product-sensitive regressions early. also let's add a test asserting no >2 BLEU drop per-locale for new quant candidates.

leo: noted. closing loop: created ML-TR-972, linked evals and artifacts. assigning: maya (triage), sam (quant patch), jin (product validation).

maya: thanks — will update thread with repro CSV and PR link. :thumbsup:
